record.paper_title: On free curves and related open problems
record.context_brief: Existence of maximal Tjurina curves and arrangements
record.original_question: For integers d ≥ 3 and r with d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−1, does there always exist a maximal Tjurina curve of type (d,r), meaning a reduced plane curve of degree d with mdr(f)=r that attains the sharpened du Plessis–Wall upper bound for the total Tjurina number? In addition, when d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−2, does there always exist a maximal Tjurina line arrangement of type (d,r)?

evidence.quote: A reduced curve C : f = 0 of degree d, such that r = mdr(f) and the equality (6.1) holds for C is called a maximal Tjurina curve of type (d, r).

Conjecture 6.1. For any integer d ≥ 3 and for any integer r such that d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−1, there are maximal Tjurina curves of type (d, r). Moreover, for d/2 ≤ r ≤ d−2, there are maximal Tjurina line arrangements of type (d, r).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ over $\mathbb{C}$. Let $f \in S = \mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $d \geq 3$ defining a reduced plane curve $C: f=0$. Let $J_f = (f_x, f_y, f_z)$ be the Jacobian ideal, and let $\mathrm{AR}(f) = \{(a,b,c) \in S^3 : a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0\}$ be the module of Jacobian syzygies. Define
$$\mathrm{mdr}(f) = \min\{q \geq 0 : \mathrm{AR}(f)_q \neq 0\},$$
the minimal degree of a nontrivial Jacobian relation. Let $\tau(C) = \dim_{\mathbb{C}} S/(f, f_x, f_y, f_z)$ denote the total Tjurina number (sum of local Tjurina numbers at the singularities of $C$).

The (sharpened) du Plessis–Wall upper bound asserts that for $r = \mathrm{mdr}(f)$ with $r \leq (d-1)/2$ or $r \geq (d-1)/2$, one has
$$\tau(C) \leq \tau(d,r)_{\max} := (d-1)(d-r-1) + r^2 - \binom{2r-d+2}{2}_+,$$
where $\binom{m}{2}_+ = \binom{m}{2}$ if $m \geq 0$ and $0$ otherwise. A reduced curve $C$ of degree $d$ with $\mathrm{mdr}(f) = r$ for which $\tau(C) = \tau(d,r)_{\max}$ is called a maximal Tjurina curve of type $(d,r)$. If in addition $C$ is a union of $d$ distinct lines, it is called a maximal Tjurina line arrangement of type $(d,r)$.

Question:
(a) For every integer $d \geq 3$ and every integer $r$ with $d/2 \leq r \leq d-1$, does there exist a maximal Tjurina curve of type $(d,r)$?
(b) For every integer $d \geq 3$ and every integer $r$ with $d/2 \leq r \leq d-2$, does there exist a maximal Tjurina line arrangement of type $(d,r)$?

artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been verified for many pairs (d,r), in particular for all admissible pairs with d ≤ 11, and recent work has established the existence of maximal Tjurina line arrangements in many new situations. However, the general case (especially for curves with d/2 < r ≤ d−2) remains open.

status_evidence.title: Jacobian syzygies and plane curves with maximal global Tjurina numbers
status_evidence.snippet: Studies plane curves attaining the du Plessis–Wall bound; introduces maximal Tjurina curves of type (d,r).
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework and proves existence in many cases.

status_evidence.title: Addition–deletion results ... maximal Tjurina line arrangements
status_evidence.snippet: Proves existence of maximal Tjurina line arrangements in numerous new cases via addition-deletion techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on the line-arrangement part of the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On free curves and related open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the conjecture and notes it is verified for all admissible pairs with d ≤ 11.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains open in general but verified for small degree.
